### Ion packing and the Born diameters

All 21 single-sphere ion declarations in the 4 records satisfy $d=0.88\sigma$. Every Debye–Hückel diameter equals the segment diameter. DEAH⁺ and MDEAH⁺ use temperature-dependent hard-chain packing, with their Debye–Hückel and Born diameters tied to the segment diameter.

Held et al. (2014), §2.4 Eq. (21), insert the 0.88 factor in the packing term, with zero ion self-dispersion in Eq. (22). Their §2.1 uses the solvated-ion segment diameter for Debye–Hückel. Figiel et al. (2025), Eq. (4), use the packing diameter in Debye–Hückel. Schick et al. (2023), p. 3, use $d=\sigma$. Held fitted osmotic coefficients and densities at 298.15 K without a Born contribution and lists no carbonate salt in Table 5. Its Table 2 ties the interactions to its water parameters. Figiel refitted ion–water and ion–ion interactions. Its new pure-ion fits were V³⁺ and VO²⁺ (p. 9410), and it fitted solvation factors for water, methanol and ethanol (pp. 9411, 9413). M3 uses an assumed MEA factor.

| Cation | Segments | Born diameter (Å) | Volume-equivalent diameter (Å) | Parent (Å) | Classical continuum Born energy (kJ/mol) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MEAH⁺ | 1 | 4.856 | 4.856 | 4.407 | -282.48 |
| DEAH⁺ | 5.2048 | 2.948 | 5.108 | 5.108 | -465.33 |
| MDEAH⁺ | 3.675 | 3.655 | 5.641 | 5.498 | -375.25 |
| AMPH⁺ | 1 | 6.469 | 6.469 | 5.091 | -212.02 |

Classical continuum energies use the tied Born diameter and model water permittivity 78.49894463 at 298.15 K and 101325 Pa. The Engine's SSM+DS contribution adds an outer-shell correction. AMPH⁺ has bounds 4.5–6.5 Å (inactive) and conditional standard error 0.322 Å. The table uses 45 NaHCO₃, 45 Na₂CO₃ and 39 mixed rows per case. Negative charge-closure OH⁻ left 6 mixed rows unavailable. Peiper and Pitzer (1982), Table 6, supplies model-derived values at 278.15–318.15 K and 0.01–1 mol/kg. AARD uses the corrected ionic reference as its denominator after charge closure and ideal removal of dissolved CO₂ at 0.1 MPa. N1 uses the NaCl-fitted water–Na⁺ intercept. N2 uses Held's published temperature law. Held's Table 5 strategy 2 reports 2.41% for Na₂SO₄ and 6.43% for Na₂HPO₄ under its own formulation. The difference between sodium laws limits attribution to the shared pairs. [Row residuals by molality](results/shared-ion-electrostatics-423/c9fbf898b14d004f915f01ed77675867908dd30d77dc28544b2860e9195c80bb/ae17803e1bcb2ca0a1970e05c7cc235d615c4d8a3a349b5afef0b0401dedefed/N1/F2/osmotic.json), [temperature summaries](results/shared-ion-electrostatics-423/c9fbf898b14d004f915f01ed77675867908dd30d77dc28544b2860e9195c80bb/ae17803e1bcb2ca0a1970e05c7cc235d615c4d8a3a349b5afef0b0401dedefed/N1/F2/summary.json).

The N1 reactive control uses CO₂–Na⁺ $k=0$, nominal salt per kilogram of water, and an electroneutral dilution path of 0.125 per non-sodium solute and 0.375 for Na⁺ at standard molality 1 mol/kg and pressure 0.1 MPa. At 298.15 K, the molality-basis R2 and R3 pK values are 6.35908 and 10.33280, compared with Peiper and Pitzer's 6.355 and 10.337. Each set scores 36 salt rows and retains 24 outside the R2 range. Printed bare zeros have no rounding score.

The largest geometric mean is 0.04022 for [carbonate-anion-4.953](results/shared-ion-electrostatics-423/c9fbf898b14d004f915f01ed77675867908dd30d77dc28544b2860e9195c80bb/ae17803e1bcb2ca0a1970e05c7cc235d615c4d8a3a349b5afef0b0401dedefed/carbonate-anion-4.953/carbonate-share.json), 1.269 times F2 over 10 matched states and 24.9-fold below the source values. The carbonate share is excluded from the fit. Jakobsen reports limited NMR resolution below roughly 10% of a common signal. The local refits and finite searches describe these observations and trial banks. They provide no global stability guarantee.

S1 is the jointly refitted negative record from #396. It costs 151.787333918 on the original objective and 158.856886364 on the joint objective. Admission retained 10/10 shares (5 at 293.15 K and 5 at 313.15 K, at 101325 Pa). The search was incomplete at 10/10 parents. 10 trial banks have unsuccessful optimizers. States 018 and 021 also have explicitly unresolved trials. State 019 has an unconfirmed descent. The remaining 9 searches have unresolved dispositions. | P0-refit | 150.762902879547 | 150.766713874310 | previous | no | +0.00000000 | yes |
| P1-refit | 150.871225577284 | 150.871328025253 | previous | yes | +0.10832270 | no |
| M3-refit | 149.667373714297 | 149.667331508646 | current | yes | -1.09557137 | no |

The cross-arm tie rule uses relative cost difference 1e-06 from the lower endpoint. M3's lowest converged local fit reduces the cost by 1.096 relative to P0's refit and lowers the geometric-mean carbonate share ratio from 0.0316987 to 0.0197306. The selected fits have active bounds on pair/carbamate-anion/protonated-monoethanolamine/k_ij. The F2 information record lists 4 conditional correlation pairs with absolute values above 0.95. [Coordinates, active bounds and conditional correlations](results/shared-ion-electrostatics-423/c9fbf898b14d004f915f01ed77675867908dd30d77dc28544b2860e9195c80bb/ae17803e1bcb2ca0a1970e05c7cc235d615c4d8a3a349b5afef0b0401dedefed/refit-comparison.json).

The timed first P0 fit took 65.0 s (converged). The P0 endpoint search took 692.1 s and evaluated 991,602 supplied trials. These are individual wall-clock runs with at most 3 workers and single-threaded numerical libraries. [Retained wheel and F2 record directory](results/shared-ion-electrostatics-423/c9fbf898b14d004f915f01ed77675867908dd30d77dc28544b2860e9195c80bb/ae17803e1bcb2ca0a1970e05c7cc235d615c4d8a3a349b5afef0b0401dedefed/controls.json)

### Before and after text for the manuscript handoff

- **P:theory-02a**
  - Before. “A single-sphere ion has the temperature-independent diameter $d_i=0.88\sigma_i$.”
  - After. A single-sphere ion has the packing diameter $d_i=0.88\sigma_i$ (Held et al., 2014, Eq. 21). The Debye–Hückel closest-approach diameter is $\sigma_i$ (Held et al., §2.1). Figiel et al. (2025, p. 9407) use the packing diameter in Debye–Hückel.

- **P:theory-04**
  - Before. “Figiel et al. restrict the average … to ions and solvents; here it runs over all components.”
  - After. The average includes molecular CO₂ with unit solvation factor. Figiel’s Eq. 9 averages ions and solvents. The present model assigns the amine unit solvation factor, and Figiel fitted solvent factors for water, methanol and ethanol. Raising the CO₂ factor to 1.5 at fixed coefficients changes cost by +0.569. Raising the MEA factor to 1.5 changes fixed-coefficient cost by +15.037. M3's lowest converged local fit reduces the cost by 1.096 relative to P0's refit and lowers the geometric-mean carbonate share ratio from 0.0316987 to 0.0197306. The exact solvent-and-ion average is pending.

- **P:theory-permittivity-inputs and P:supplement-20**
  - Before. “At the measurement temperature, two coefficient pairs give identical permittivities at any density.”
  - After. The pairs (0.73099 L/mol, 1019.08 K) and (0.24645 L/mol, 2436.44 K) give the same permittivity at 298.15 K. At 313.15, 353.15, 393.15 K in unloaded 30 wt% MEA, the smaller-volume pair raises $\varepsilon-1$ by 0.19%, 0.71%, 1.28%, respectively, at fixed density.

- **P:theory-amine-species and tab:transfer-species**
  - Before. “For every amine ion the Debye–Hückel and Born diameters equal the segment diameter.”
  - After. The Debye–Hückel and Born diameters equal the segment diameter. The volume-equivalent diameters, $\sigma m^{1/3}$, are 4.856 Å for MEAH⁺, 5.108 Å for DEAH⁺, 5.641 Å for MDEAH⁺, 6.469 Å for AMPH⁺. Include the volume-equivalent values alongside the tied Born diameters in the transfer species table.

- **P:supplement-18 and P:supplement-shared**
  - Before. “The Born diameters of bicarbonate and carbonate are set here at 3.0 Å.”
  - After. The carbonate-share table gives the pressure, objective and share responses across both Born diameter brackets. Report the sodium-salt comparisons with the Peiper–Pitzer ionic reference basis, both sodium laws, and the tested range.

- **MEA results and Jakobsen carbonate figure caption**
  - Before. “The small share cannot be attributed to a single parameter, and the fitted pressures do not determine this minor-species partition.”
  - After. The 10 carbonate fractions give a geometric-mean calculated-to-observed ratio of 0.0317. In water, with the declared sodium interactions and CO₂–Na⁺ $k=0$, the reactive sodium-salt comparisons also exceed print rounding. The cause of the MEA deficit remains unresolved.

Use the retained values as inputs to the existing number display producers and their readback in #429.
